Shapes

This example creates the shapes of Geom4hep, calls the shape functions on them and draws them. The shapes have the parameters of the corresponding Geant4 solids.

Note that

You can also download this example as a Jupyter notebook and a plain Julia source file.

Table of contents

  • Loading the modules
  • Creating shapes
  • Drawing shapes
  • Shape functions
  • Checking the distances
  • Boolean shapes
  • Single precision

Loading the modules

CairoMakie draws into images; use GLMakie instead for interactive windows. Makie exports names that are also shapes of Geom4hep (e.g. Box), so only the names that are needed are imported from it.

using Geom4hep, Geom4hep.Units
using LinearAlgebra
using CairoMakie: CairoMakie, Figure, LScene

const T = Float64;

Creating shapes

The constructors take the floating point type as parameter, and the parameters of the shape with the conventions of the Geant4 solids: half lengths, radii, and angular ranges given by a start angle and an extent. Lengths are in mm and angles in radians; the units of Geom4hep.Units make this explicit.

box    = Box{T}(10cm, 15cm, 20cm)
tube   = Tube{T}(5cm, 10cm, 20cm, 0, 270deg)
cone   = Cone{T}(2cm, 5cm, 5cm, 10cm, 20cm, 0, 2π)
trd    = Trd{T}(10cm, 5cm, 15cm, 8cm, 20cm)
trap   = Trap{T}(20cm, 10deg, 30deg, 10cm, 8cm, 12cm, 5deg, 6cm, 5cm, 7cm, 5deg)
sphere = Sphere{T}(8cm, 10cm, 0, 270deg, 30deg, 120deg)
torus  = Torus{T}(2cm, 4cm, 12cm, 0, 270deg)
pcone  = Polycone{T}([0, 5cm, 5cm, 0], [8cm, 10cm, 10cm, 6cm], [-20cm, -10cm, 10cm, 20cm], 0, 2π)
phedra = Polyhedra{T}(6, [3cm, 3cm, 3cm], [6cm, 10cm, 6cm], [-20cm, 0, 20cm], 0, 2π)
ctube  = CutTube{T}(5cm, 10cm, 20cm, 0, 2π, Vector3{T}(0, -0.5, -1), Vector3{T}(0.5, 0, 1));

Printing a shape shows its parameters

torus
Torus{Float64}(rmin = 20.0, rmax = 40.0, rtor = 120.0, ϕ₀ = 0.0, Δϕ = 4.71238898038469)

Drawing shapes

With a Makie backend loaded, draw(shape) creates a figure with the shape, and draw! adds it to a scene. Here all the shapes are drawn in a grid.

shapes = [box, tube, cone, trd, trap, sphere, torus, pcone, phedra, ctube]
fig = Figure(size=(1000, 450))
for (i, s) in enumerate(shapes)
    scene = LScene(fig[(i-1) ÷ 5 + 1, (i-1) % 5 + 1], show_axis=false)
    draw!(scene, s)
end
fig

Shape functions

The shape functions take points and directions in the frame of the shape. inside classifies a point as kInside, kSurface or kOutside:

p_in, p_out = Point3{T}(0, 0, 0), Point3{T}(30cm, 0, 0)
inside(box, p_in) == kInside, inside(box, p_out) == kOutside, inside(box, Point3{T}(10cm, 0, 0)) == kSurface
(true, true, true)

distance_to_in is the distance along a direction from an outside point to the shape, and distance_to_out from an inside point to the surface:

dir = Vector3{T}(-1, 0, 0)
distance_to_in(box, p_out, dir), distance_to_out(box, p_in, dir)
(200.0, 100.0)

A ray that misses the shape gets Inf:

distance_to_in(box, p_out, Vector3{T}(0, 1, 0))
Inf

The safeties are lower bounds of the distance to the surface in any direction:

safety_to_in(box, p_out), safety_to_out(box, Point3{T}(5cm, 0, 0))
(200.0, 50.0)

normal gives the outward normal at a point of the surface, extent the corners of a bounding box, and capacity and surface the volume and the area:

normal(sphere, Point3{T}(0, 10cm, 0))
3-element Geom4hep.Vector3{Float64} with indices SOneTo(3):
 0.0
 1.0
 0.0
extent(torus)
([-160.0, -160.0, -40.0], [160.0, 160.0, 40.0])
capacity(box) ≈ 8 * 10cm * 15cm * 20cm, surface(box)
(true, 520000.0)

Checking the distances

draw_distance_to_in shoots random rays from outside a shape and draws the points where they enter it; draw_distance_to_out does the same from inside. Both draw the surface of the shape, which is a good visual test of the distance functions.

draw_distance_to_out(phedra, 50_000)

Boolean shapes

Boolean shapes combine two shapes; the second one is placed in the frame of the first one with a Transformation3D. They can be nested.

hole  = Tube{T}(0, 4cm, 30cm, 0, 2π)
frame = BooleanSubtraction(box, hole)
frame = BooleanSubtraction(frame, hole, Transformation3D{T}(0, 0, 0, π/2, 0, 0))
frame = BooleanUnion(frame, Sphere{T}(0, 6cm), Transformation3D{T}(0, 0, 20cm))
inside(frame, Point3{T}(0, 0, 0)) == kOutside, inside(frame, Point3{T}(0, 0, 24cm)) == kInside
(true, true)

The rays shot by draw_distance_to_in show the result:

draw_distance_to_in(frame, 50_000)

Single precision

All the shapes can also be created in single precision, which is what most GPUs need. The surfaces are then thicker (tolerance(Float32) is 1 µm) to absorb the rounding errors.

box32 = Box{Float32}(10cm, 15cm, 20cm)
distance_to_in(box32, Point3{Float32}(30cm, 0, 0), Vector3{Float32}(-1, 0, 0)), tolerance(Float32)
(200.0f0, 0.001f0)
